body_text:
Categoricity of the Real Continuum. Up to a unique
order-preserving field isomorphism, there exists exactly one
complete ordered field.

Consequently, the concrete models of the real numbers—whether
realized via Dedekind cuts in $\mathbb{Q}$, Cantor equivalence
classes of rational Cauchy sequences, or positional decimal
expansions—are all mutually isomorphic as ordered fields. The
specific set-theoretic construction serves solely as an existence
proof of the structure; the deductive theorems of analysis depend
exclusively on the universal axiomatic properties of the complete
ordered field $\mathbb{R}$.
